01 · Cover
Cue: Arriving here clears the session clock. → turns the globe into a map; → again opens the cold open. Shift+R brings you back here from any slide (R alone does nothing).
Say: “Good morning. Today we prepare one company for an audit. You play, Claude does the work, and I keep score.”
Interaction: Names or team names on the game sheets.
Fallback: No sheets? Paper and pen work: the game is on the slides too.
Before the session: run every prompt once in your own Claude with the kit's Project. The answer key on the slides is the kit's ANSWERS.md, not a recording of a Claude run. Open five tabs: Step 1 to Step 4 as new chats in the Project, and Step 5 as a new chat with the Step 4 table pasted under the prompt (the fallback).

02 · Cold open
Cue: No build steps. The note types itself, a pencil line marks “all patient data stays in the EU”, then the question appears. Do not resolve it here: it comes back on slide 16.
Say: “The Head of Operations sends you this note. She is about to fill in the audit answers. Would you send her sentence to the auditor as it is?”
Interaction: Thumbs up or down. Say what you see: “Mostly up” or “Mostly down: suspicious already, good.” Write it on your run sheet; you need it on slide 16. Then: “Keep your answer, we'll come back to it.”
Fallback: Quiet room? Ask a pair, not a person: “What does this note assume?”

03 · Host
Cue: → → for the career line, then on. 20 to 30 seconds. The words dated, signed and in one place are underlined as the line passes.
Say: “I'm Tim. I build data systems and use Claude every day. An audit asks for evidence you already have, with a deadline.”
Interaction: None: the room listens.
Fallback: Running late? Press through and say only the last sentence.

04 · Why now
Cue: Ask for hands before the first →. Three →: customers, certifiers, the law, each with a count tag. The fourth → draws all three into one slab: one folder of dated evidence.
Say: “A processor has to allow audits by its customer (GDPR Art. 28). A certificate for ISO 27001 typically runs three years, with a check audit every year. North Macedonia's data law follows the GDPR, and the EU AI Act asks firms to support their staff's AI literacy. One folder of dated evidence can answer all three.”
Interaction: Hands up: who has been asked for proof by a customer, an auditor or a bank this year?
Fallback: No hands? “Who expects one next year?” Do not explain the AI Act in depth: say that drafting audit answers with an AI tool is allowed and that this workshop is about the evidence, not the law. Not legal advice.

05 · The thread
Cue: Four →: the request lights up with its file, the thread runs through ticket and systems, it reaches the log and breaks: the proof slot stays empty and NO PROOF lands on it. Then the closing question.
Say: “An auditor doesn't read everything. They pick one record and follow it. If the thread ends before a proof, that is a finding.”
Interaction: At the last press: “Where would your thread break? Keep that thought: it is the bet in Step 3.”
Fallback: Do not name the erasure case answer here: it is Step 3.

06 · The evidence test
Cue: Five →, one question each, all asked of one invented file (web_test_report_2024.txt). Each press stamps a tick or a cross and lights the line it checks. The fifth press settles the file on WEAK: two crosses, so it cannot be COVERED. COVERED and GAP stay dim until a file hits them.
Say: “Five questions turn a file into evidence: is it there, is it current, does it cover the claim, is it signed and owned, does it agree with the other files. The answers become three statuses: COVERED, WEAK, GAP.” At the legend: “COVERED can still be bad news. A file can prove that we fail a rule.”
Interaction: None: the room listens. The sample file is not in the kit, so nothing here gives away the trap hunt.
Fallback: Short on time? Read the five questions in one breath and show the legend.

07 · The case
Cue: Two →: the week pops in while the day counter rolls from 20 to 0, then Friday drops in with the fiction line. The four numbers count up, the 7 last.
Say: “Termin Health, a software company in Skopje: 31 people, 46 clinics, health data. Rheinland Praxisverbund audits it on Thursday 3 December. Today is 13 November. Monday a document request, Tuesday seven claims, Wednesday the auditor follows one record, Thursday one passport, Friday one more surprise. The company is invented, the laws are real.” Point at the small line: GDPR Art. 28 and 44 to 46, ISO 27001 Annex A and AI Act Art. 4 are the rules in play, summarised in audit_topics_reference.md. Not legal advice.
Interaction: None: the room listens.
Fallback: Never say “invoice” or “photo” here: the room bets on it in Step 5.

08 · Setup
Cue: Four →: rule 1, rule 2, rule 3, then the 13 files. Five files get a red square (traps on your cards), two an outlined square (Claude finds them), and the backup test a tick (the clean file). COPY INSTRUCTIONS on the card copies the full project instructions.
Say: “One Project: 13 company files, two dates, three rules. Even AI legal research tools hallucinated in 17 to 33% of queries in a 2025 study, so a person checks every answer. Seven traps and one clean file are hidden in this folder: five are on your cards, and Claude finds the other two.”
Interaction: Make pairs: the Hunter leads the trap hunt and the bets, the Auditor checks Claude's sources.
Fallback: Odd number of people? One trio, with two Auditors. Fewer than 6 people? No pairs or roles: everyone plays solo, and the room plays against Claude.

09 · Spot the trap
Cue: Arriving here starts the session clock: the chip top right is your timer. FIRST switch to tab 1, send Prompt 1, come back, then say “Go”. → is “Go”: it starts the 3:00 bar and shows the points rule.
Say: “Claude has just started reading the same files. Five of the seven traps are on these cards; one card is clean. Mark each on your sheet. Three minutes. The strip at the bottom explains DPA, MFA, pen test and out of scope. Go.”
Interaction: Pairs tick Trap or Clean on each card and write one word under “Why?”. When the bar turns red (2:00 gone): “One minute left.” At 0:00 on the bar (3:00 gone): “Pens down. No changes after this.”
Fallback: Prompt 1 will not send? Try once more, then switch to the hotspot. The hunt goes on either way.

10 · Step 1 · Document request
Cue: Step 0 is the bet: the eight topics are in the bet box. Press → ONLY once Claude's table is visible in tab 1: the bet list flies into the table rows. Then one → per panel: the tally, D5 training, D6 and D7, D8 the clean file (Attempt 1, Fix, Attempt 2 draw one after the other), the traps line.
Say: Bet: “Rheinland asks eight things. How many does Claude mark COVERED? Write your number.” At the table: “Closest bet wins.” At the tally: “Three COVERED, four WEAK, one GAP. Two of the COVERED carry bad news: the file proves that we fail a rule. That is still COVERED, plus an action.” At D8: “The first restore attempt failed. It is explained, fixed and retested, so it is evidence, not a problem.” At the traps line: “Five tickets with patient names in the Claude workspace, and the training shares. Claude found both. Spotted one before Claude did? Say so to your neighbour.”
Interaction: Everyone writes a number. Score: exact 2, off by one 1; trap cards 1 to 5 and the clean card 6.
Fallback: No table by 0:08 on the session clock? Say “Claude is slow today”, press → and use the kit's answer key. Claude differs from the slide? Compare statuses and numbers with ANSWERS.md and read its reason: a different status with a good reason is a good catch.

11 · Step 2 · Trust page
Cue: Send Prompt 2 in tab 2 first (attach inbox/2-trust-page-claims.md). Step 0 is the vote. → underlines the red words and stacks the red evidence, → the amber ones, → the green one and a safe rewrite beside claim 1. Wait for the revote before the next →.
Say: “Red: the files say no. Amber: not fully proven. Green: a file proves every word.” At claim 3: “Every EU statement in the files traces back to one sales page. Keep that in mind for Step 5.”
Interaction: Cards up for each claim, 60 seconds with the neighbour, then a revote on the most split claim (usually 3 and 4). Score: 1 per right colour; trap cards 1 and 4 (claim 6 is the MFA line on card 4). Claim 5, the training shares, is a trap Claude finds: it is on no card.
Fallback: Claude slow? The vote fills the time. Still nothing at 0:15? Use the slide's verdicts, and say so. Asked about “GDPR compliant” as a claim? It is not in the list, and it is a legal conclusion that no folder of files can prove: the safe pattern is to state facts.

12 · Data, Place, Paper
Cue: Send nothing to Claude here. Three →: the GO files, the CLEAN FIRST files, the STAY OUT file, then the closing line. Each press slides the cards into their lane and tags them with the question that decided it. The three questions are on screen from arrival.
Say: “Before any file goes into an AI tool, ask three things: Data, Place, Paper. What is in the file? Where does the tool run, who runs the machine, what do its logs keep, who can log in? And what allows it: a contract, retention and training terms, your own policy?” At the end: “A data processing agreement answers Paper only. Data and Place still decide.”
Interaction: Everyone sorts the six files on the sheet (3 minutes: alone first, then compare with a neighbour), then → reveals the lanes. Score: 1 point per file in the right lane. Common dispute: file 3 and file 6 are CLEAN FIRST (file 6: bucket names and project ID reveal where your data is stored) because the real versions hold names, emails or account IDs.
Fallback: Out of time? Reveal all lanes in three presses and move on. Everything in this kit is invented, so nothing uploaded here is a problem: the habit is the point.

13 · Step 3 · Trace
Cue: Send Prompt 3 in tab 3 first (attach inbox/3-erasure-request.md). Step 0 is the bet: one place on the sheet. At about 0:24 on the session clock start Prompt 4 in tab 4 (the cooking show) and note the time you send it: the room bets on Claude's time in Step 4 (the kit allows 3 to 6 minutes). Then → once the table is visible: seven places, the policy line, the numbers, the verdict.
Say: “The clinic asked on 2 September and we confirmed on 21 September: all data deleted. Where will the thread break?” At the policy: “The policy lists three places and adds the backups. The exports bucket, the Claude workspace and the model's log are not in it.” At the verdict: “The deadline was met. The sentence was not true.”
Interaction: Everyone marks one place before the table. Score, as on the sheet: 2 points for a place with no proof (4, 5 or 6), 1 for a weak one (1, 2 or 3), 0 for backups (7): the backups are COVERED.
Fallback: Claude says the triage log is WEAK? Nothing proves the patient is absent and the log is never deleted, so GAP. Claude slow? Use the slide at 0:25.
Timing (whole session, 60 minutes; the session clock starts at slide 9, minute 8): cover and context 0 to 8, trap hunt 8 to 13, Steps 1 and 2 13 to 28, Data, Place, Paper 28 to 32, Step 3 32 to 40, Step 4 40 to 50, Step 5 50 to 55, close 55 to 60. Behind by 5 minutes? Skip the revote in Step 2 and read the exit ticket in one round.

14 · Step 4 · Passport
Cue: Step 0 is the two bets. Press → ONLY after Claude's table is on screen in tab 4, and say how many minutes it took since you sent it. Then one → per panel: the tiles, the training chart (a bonus in the kit), the seven lights from Step 2, the closing list, the volunteer. The slide is the answer key.
Say: “Twelve topics: two COVERED, five WEAK, five GAP. The weakest part decides, so a missing contract, DPIA, mechanism or procedure makes the topic a GAP.” At the list: “Every WEAK and GAP names the document that would close it.”
Interaction: Bet 1, 1 point: how many topics are COVERED. Bet 2, 2 points: Claude's time for the passport table: under 2, 2 to 4, or over 4 minutes. While Claude builds: page 2 of the sheet. Volunteer: one person answers the auditor's question from the files: name the gap, the owner and the date.
Fallback: No table by 0:31? Go through the slide and say “This is the kit's answer key.”

15 · Step 5 · Invoice
Cue: Claude first, then the bet. Click Copy on the prompt card, switch to tab 4 (the Step 4 chat), attach the invoice with the paperclip, paste, send, come back. Tab 4 still working? Send tab 5 (the fallback with your table pasted under the prompt) at once. Step 0 is the bet. Press → to step 1 only after Claude has named the data centre; show that line first. Leaving this slide forward stops the session clock.
Say: At step 1: “This is a phone photo. Claude read the data centre: US-East, Ashburn, Virginia. The server was created on 27 March.” At step 2: “231 days. The invoice proves the US data centre for October. If the server never moved, the model that the policy puts in our EU environment has run in the USA for all 231 days. The files do not show how many of those days it held patient data.” At step 3: “One status changes, eight stay the same: claim 3 turns red. A4 was already GAP and only gets a worse reason.” At step 4: “No answer got better. Audit preparation finds bad news early.”
Interaction: Thumbs: up = a status changes, down = only a reason changes. Score: up = 2 points. Whether this is a personal data breach is a legal question for the data protection contact: say so if asked.
Fallback: Usage limit or slow? Go through the slide (the kit's answer key), or use tab 5. Never cut this step.

16 · Would you send it now?
Cue: You arrive on the note from minute one. → strikes the false sentence and shows where patient data sits.
Say: “At minute one, [say what you wrote down] for this note. Frankfurt holds the database, the PDFs and the backups. The exports bucket and the triage server are in the USA. Would you send it now?” Then: “No. Now every sentence has a file behind it, and that is what COVERED means.”
Interaction: Thumbs again.
Fallback: Step 5 did not run live? Use the slide: “This is the kit's answer key.” Same question.

17 · Five facts
Cue: Five →, one fact each; the last press adds the closing line.
Say: “Open weights is not a location. You can download the model, and you still have to write down where it runs. Model, version and licence: missing. Who runs the machine: recorded. Which country: wrong, the sales page said EU. Logs: every prompt, never deleted. Who can log in: recorded. Fact 3 is the one that hid it: the server is in the USA, and it has existed for 231 days.” At the end: “For a hosted assistant, ask the vendor for the contract and the region. The same five facts apply.”
Interaction: None. Optional: “Which of the five facts would you write down first for your own tool?”
Fallback: Running late? Read facts 1 and 3 only.

18 · Exit ticket
Cue: Read a line, cards up, then → stamps its answer. Three times.
Say: Line 1: WEAK. Line 2: GAP, and name the document that would prove it. Line 3: COVERED, plus an action. “1 point per right card.”
Interaction: Cards or thumbs: up = COVERED, sideways = WEAK, down = GAP.
Fallback: Running late? Read all three, one round of cards, then → → →.

19 · Close
Cue: Three →: the 12 topics, the Monday list (find three things in 10 minutes; the first one you cannot find is your first gap: a contract, an AI tool, an old document), the kit with its short URL and the QR code. Shift+R goes back to the cover and clears the clock.
Say: “Highest score: a prize and applause; no need to stand.” “Page 2 of your sheet is your Monday. The kit is your homework: allow about 2 hours the first time; you can stop after any step.” “The kit runs on Free; for real company work a paid plan gives more usage. Check Settings > Privacy first, and never upload real patient data.” Last line: “Find the gap before the auditor does. And a person on your team still checks every answer before it goes out.”
Interaction: Winner and applause. “My plan”: “Write the name of the next customer or auditor who will ask you. 60 seconds.” Then questions.
Fallback: No time left? “Ask me after the session.” End on time.
